status_summary: In May 2025 the acting head of the Bureau of African Affairs launched a Commercial Diplomacy Strategy, framed as trade not aid, whose six actions include working with governments in priority countries, defined as those where US companies want to do business and data support it, and backing infrastructure projects in those countries. The National Security Strategy released 2025-12-04 calls for a transition in Africa from a foreign aid paradigm to an investment and growth paradigm favoring capable, reliable states, but names no focus country list. In December 2025 the State Department signed health compacts with eight African governments, and on 2026-02-03 the President signed legislation reauthorizing AGOA through 2026-12-31, retroactive to 2025-09-30.

timeline.event: The Bureau of African Affairs launched a Commercial Diplomacy Strategy with six actions, including reforms and infrastructure projects in priority countries, announced by the acting head of the bureau at a business summit in Abidjan. (month only; first of month used)

The State Department signed bilateral health memorandums of understanding with eight sub-Saharan African governments (Cameroon, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Mozambique, Rwanda and Uganda), beginning with Kenya, under the America First Global Health Strategy. (month only; first of month used)
The White House released the National Security Strategy, which calls for a shift in Africa from aid to trade and investment and refers only generally to select partner states.
The President signed legislation reauthorizing the African Growth and Opportunity Act through 2026-12-31, retroactive to 2025-09-30.

title: Shift Africa policy from aid to private-sector growth with designated focus countries
uncertainties: The public law number for the AGOA reauthorization was not confirmed; the USTR statement does not cite one. The Commercial Diplomacy Strategy speech was read on a news aggregator that prints no date, so the month rests on that page's story identifier. The priority-country concept in the commercial strategy is the nearest match to the Mandate's focus countries, but it is limited to commercial engagement and no list was found. The eight health compacts are a global health selection, not a general focus-country designation, and their individual signing dates were not confirmed. The end of USAID programs in Africa and any 2025 Africa summit were not separately researched. The aid-to-growth element overlaps c09-17 (Prosper Africa and the USAID, DFC and Commerce toolkit); the focus-country element does not appear there.
